reuse.why: The change reuses getApproxNumberThreshold and updates getScheduledAmount, but the API independently implements amount resolution and approximate resolution remains outside the shared helper.

duplication.why: The API's missing, numeric, and ranged amount dispatch duplicates the decision already owned by getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: Shared ranged resolution is appropriately placed, but expected-amount policy also lives in API serialization and budget template orchestration.

scope.why: All edits concern expected schedule amounts, their API representation, or directly related tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate multiple amount-resolution implementations, while approximate policy is confined to one consumer instead of the shared schedule abstraction.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts: scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount directly instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: scheduleModel.toExternal reshapes getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range decision into a nested ternary.

abstraction_drift.where: api-models.ts independently resolves expectedAmount; schedule-template.ts adds an isapprox branch and tolerance subtraction outside getScheduledAmount, leaving the shared helper without operator-aware resolution.
